maya: Quick note — pulled a perfetto trace for the 1.2.0 rollout on dedicated that shows the kernel selector flipping kernels mid-request for batch=8 seq=1024. Visible spikes in GPU active time and L2 misses.

ash: Yep saw similar on prod-dedicated-04 this morning, latency tail jumped ~20%. I have an nsys capture too.

lukas: Can you paste the perfetto timeline link? I want to see the NVTX lanes.

maya: https://perfetto.local/trace/abc123 (private) — timeline shows alternating "kernel_choice" NVTX markers: fused_attn -> fused_attn_scalar -> fused_attn_fast -> fused_attn_scalar in the same request.

anya: That pattern screams selector oscillation. We added a tokens-per-kernel heuristic last sprint; maybe the moving average window is too short.

ash: Attaching short nsys snippet:
```
# nsys summary
Kernel Name                         Calls   Total Time (ms)  Avg (ms)
fused_attn_fast                      124     85.2              0.687
fused_attn_scalar                    210     132.5             0.631
fused_attn                            56     47.1              0.841
```

ash: Note the scalar variant has many more invocations with small times but causes extra kernel launches + kv cache churn.

maya: I dumped KV cache read/write counters around the request — saw ~3x writes when selector flips to scalar. Likely different memory layout forces extra cache serializations.

lukas: Reproducer idea: run batch=8 seq=1024 (pad to 1024) and compare kernel selection when prefix caching enabled vs disabled. If it's cache writes, disabling prefix KV caching should reduce flips.

maya: I ran that — disabling prefix caching stabilizes on fused_attn_fast and latency tail drops back to baseline. So KV path is implicated.

perf-bot: [automated] Created perf issue: PERF-2024-189 "kernel-selector oscillation with KV writes for batch=8 seq=1024" and attached traces.

anya: Looking at kernel_selector.cc, current heuristic uses exponential moving average of tokens_per_sec with alpha=0.6 and threshold=1.1x to pick fused. If KV writes spike for scalar path, the moving avg can swing. Need hysteresis + shape key caching.

lukas: Proposed quick patch: add hysteresis on selection and a per-(model,shape) sticky_cache for 2 seconds. Pseudocode:
```
if sticky_cache.exists(shape_key) and now - sticky_ts < 2s:
  use sticky_cache[kernel]
else:
  compute score(fused) and score(scalar)
  if score(fused) > score(scalar) * (1 + hysteresis): pick fused
  else pick scalar
  update sticky_cache
```

maya: Also lowering the tokens threshold from 8192->6144 avoided flips in my local run. Might be too blunt but helps.

ash: We should also add a metric: kernel_switch_count per request and alert if > 3 for same request id. Quick dashboard to catch regressions.

anya: Agreed. Action items: 1) Lukas to draft sticky selection + hysteresis patch (PR), 2) Maya to add perf test reproducer to bench suite, 3) Ash to add kernel_switch_count metric and perf dashboard.

maya: I'll attach the perfetto screenshot and the small repro script here. repro gist: https://gist.local/repro-kernel-flip.sh

lukas: I'll push a branch tomorrow with unit tests for kernel_selector and a small E2E that runs the reproducer against the runtime binary.

ash: After patch we should run full nsys sweep across batch sizes 1,2,4,8,16 and seq lenses [256,512,1024,2048] to make sure no regressions. I'll coord with eng-sre for GPU slots.

maya: Thanks folks. If we can get the sticky selector in prodconfig quickly it should reduce the cascade of KV writes and fix the tail.

perf-bot: [automated] Linked PR PERF-2024-189 -> PR #4520 (lukas/sticky-selector)

anya: Posting retrospective note: selector oscillation is easy to miss in unit perf since aggregate numbers look fine; we need request-level histograms (kernel switch counts) to catch this class of issues earlier.

maya: End of thread — monitoring alerts set.
